newsitem.title: USA: Clinton raises chance of deal on Social Security.
newsitem.headline: Clinton raises chance of deal on Social Security.

text.p: To help balance the budget, President Clinton raised the possibility Saturday of a compromise with congressional Republicans on curbing cost-of-living increases for Social Security recipients.

Cinton, in an interview to be broadcast Sunday on CBS's "Face the Nation," said he could consider such curbs to cut spending. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott has left open the possibility of negotiating a compromise on the politically explosive issue -- if the president would consider the matter.

Lott has said he would like to see a downward adjustment in the Consumer Price Index, which is used to calculate the cost of living increases for government benefits such as Social Security, tax-rate brackets and wages.

Clinton, in the interview taped Saturday, said he could weigh such a spending curb "if it's justified." He noted that "most people believe that the cost-of-living formula the government now uses overstates the real cost of living to the people who benefit from the programmes. There is an overwhelming consensus about that."
"So, let me reiterate what I have said repeatedly: I think there ought to be a cost-of-living adjustment. But it ought to be accurate," Clinton said.

An advisory commission headed by Stanford University economist Michael Boskin late last year said the CPI overstated inflation by about 1.1 percentage points a year. A downward adjustment of that magnitude in the cost-of-living formula for people on Social Security would save the government tens of billions of dollars.
